summary: This program builds two sets of song titles — yours and a friend's — and then uses the three classic set operations to find the songs you share, the combined collection of all songs, and the songs only you have.

lines.text: Brings in the Set interface, which represents a collection that refuses to hold duplicates and does not promise any particular order.
Declares the variable by its interface (Set) but creates a HashSet object, the standard fast implementation; coding to the interface makes it easy to swap in a different set later.
Adds a title to the set. If you added the same title twice, the second call would simply be ignored, which is exactly the behaviour that makes a set right for this job.
Creates the second set so the two playlists can be compared against each other.

Passing a collection to the HashSet constructor makes a copy of it. The copy matters because the set operations that follow modify the set they are called on, and you do not want to damage the original playlist.
Keeps only the elements that also appear in friendTitles and discards the rest, which leaves the songs both playlists share.
The \n prints a blank line first to separate this output from anything above it, and the set is converted to readable text like [Respect] automatically.
Starts a fresh copy of your playlist, since the previous copy has already been shrunk down to the intersection.
Pours every one of your friend's titles into the copy. Because sets reject duplicates, "Respect" appears just once in the result.
Yet another untouched copy, because computing the difference will also change the set in place.
Deletes every title your friend also owns, leaving only the songs unique to your playlist.
